messages:
refactor: share RFC 6902 equality with the toolkit's other modules

Equality of two JSON values, as RFC 6902, section 4.6 defines it, was private
to `json-patch.ts`, where only `test` needed it. The diff that follows needs the
same reading of that section, of every pair of values it considers, so it moves
to `json-value.ts` and is exported for the toolkit's own use, as dl-007 has the
modules share an internal: one reading of the section in the library, and no
copy of it in a second module.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: produce a JSON Patch between two versions of a document

`createPatch(from, to)` returns the RFC 6902 patch that turns one document into
the other, so that a client holding both sends what changed rather than the
whole new version.

The patch names only the locations the two versions disagree about: objects are
compared member by member, arrays element by element as an edit script — so an
element they share is kept wherever it moved to — and a subtree they share stops
the comparison where it starts. It holds `add`, `remove` and `replace` only.

Both documents are copied up front, as `applyMergePatch` copies its two
arguments: the values the patch carries are nobody else's, and the copy is where
the JSON data model is checked, naming which of the two documents was not JSON.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: say that a diff has no failure to catch

The README's new section named the `TypeError` for a document outside the JSON
data model but left a reader to infer the rest. `createPatch` cannot fail, and
publishes no error class for the same reason `applyMergePatch` does not (dl-016),
which is worth stating where a caller coming from `applyPatch` looks for the
error list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
